title: Bronx building's ventilation shaft collapses after explosion: 'It was crazy' - NewsBreak
text:
By Eileen Lehpamer Dominique Jack Kirstin Cole ,
2 hours ago MOTT HAVEN, The Bronx (PIX11) — A Bronx apartment building partially collapsed on Wednesday morning after an explosion in the boiler room, according to the FDNY.
The blast caused a ventilation shaft to collapse at 207 Alexander Ave. around 8:10 a.m., officials said. No injuries were reported.
Partial collapse of apartment building in NYC after explosion: FDNY Cell phone video recorded by 18-year-old Osirus Neal shows the entire top of the chimney crumbling a few minutes after the explosion and shaft collapse.
Neal told PIX 11 News, “I was only recording because half of the building was off, and it caught me by surprise that the chimney fell. It’s crazy, I’ve never seen something like that before.”
After an afternoon meeting with multiple city agencies, Deputy Mayor of Public Safety Kaz Daughtry said engineers determined the building was structurally sound and safe for people to reoccupy, except for the F and G apartment lines closest to the ventilation shaft.
That’s about 40 apartments that need to remain vacant. As of Wednesday evening, the gas to the building was off, and the entire Mitchel Houses complex had no hot water or heat. A temporary boiler for the complex was being installed on Wednesday night.
The collapse occurred just as some parents were dropping off their kids at the nearby school, P.S. 154 Jonathan D. Hyatt Elementary School, as well as the NYCHA Mitchel Day Care Center. One witness, Diamond Freeman, told PIX11 that she heard a “big boom” moments before the scene unfolded.
More: Latest News from Around the Tri-State “When you looked out, the whole building just went boom, it fell. Then you heard another boom, and all the side of the building just fell. It was crazy. All you see is smoke.”
A spokesperson for NYCHA shared the following statement with PIX11 News.
“This morning, NYCHA joined partner agencies including FDNY, NYPD, NYCEM and DOB, as well as Con Edison, to respond to an incident at Mitchel Houses. Early reports are of an explosion in a building chimney. Fortunately, no injuries have been reported, and an investigation is underway to determine the cause of this event and the extent of any damage beyond the reported exterior damage to the chimney. Agencies are on site to ensure the safety of residents and the public.”
The American Red Cross has set up a temporary shelter for residents at a nearby community center, according to the New York City Office of Emergency Management. MTA buses are also being warranted for sheltering.
A spokesperson for the Department of Education stated that P.S. 154, Jonathan D. Hyatt Elementary School, is being utilized to support the community and provide emergency shelter.
The incident comes exactly one week after a fire in a building in the same complex left a teenage girl in critical condition and a medically induced coma, according to the FDNY and the family of the teen.
Two years ago, another apartment building collapsed in the Morris Heights neighborhood of the Bronx.
This story comprises reporting from PIX11 News reporters Dominique Jack and Kirstin Cole .
